description: MECHANISM: a `define … end` body is a `repcount` boundary EVEN WHEN the procedure is called from inside a `repeat` (issue #1155). `show_turn` is only ever called from `repeat 2 [ … ]`, yet its `repcount` is still a fault. Measured against the evaluator before the rule was written: this exact program raised `ol-repcount-outside-repeat` at `runtime` after 5 events; it now raises the same code at `semantic`, before any of them. Note what settles this and what does not: `spec/commands.md:783` ties `repcount` to the ENCLOSING `repeat`, and `spec/execution-model.md:340-342` fixes lexical frame scoping for BINDINGS — but neither spells out `repcount` across a call boundary, and `execute-internal.ts` flags its empty-per-callee repeat-turn stack as an assumption. This fixture therefore characterizes the evaluator's existing behaviour rather than deciding the open question; it was reported to `@orchestrator` at implementation time. A walk without the procedure boundary would call this program clean, so this fixture is what fails if the boundary is removed.
